findings.chapter: Ch 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
findings.evidence: "Table 5-2 — Model-selection decision: embedding vs generation model ... Verdict — embedding model: all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim) ... Selection status: recommended, pending target-corpus validation [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]"
findings.issue: The embedding-model verdict carries [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] because it depends on the ~15% MAP uplift, which is an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]. But the verdict itself ('all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim)') is a selection decision derived from a table whose three rows are all [1P][FACT] model-card values (dimension, parameter count) plus [1P][DERIVED] FLOP proxies. The [ILLUSTRATIVE] provenance is applied to the verdict, which is a non-canonical scenario choice rather than a non-canonical worked example — the Preface's own Axis-1 note says '[ILLUSTRATIVE] is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical worked example: its inputs are [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and its derived results [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', and separately that 'a hypothesis is tagged [HYPOTHESIS] (Axis 2), never [ILLUSTRATIVE] (Axis 1)' (Ch. 4 Note 1). The verdict row's status is a hypothesis about transfer to the target corpus, so it should carry [HYPOTHESIS] on the epistemic axis with the mixed-input provenance explained in prose, rather than being labelled as an ILLUSTRATIVE derivation.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the 'Verdict — embedding model' row to the epistemic status that actually applies to an unvalidated recommendation (e.g. [canonical scenario][HYPOTHESIS] or a mixed-input note plus [HYPOTHESIS]), and keep the mixed-input-provenance explanation in the derivation column, consistent with Ch. 4 Note 1's 'a hypothesis is tagged [HYPOTHESIS], never [ILLUSTRATIVE]'.
